guide: Replace the demo data: open Bills, Subscriptions and Contracts and type your own rows over the sample ones, or delete the sample rows and start with the blank copy. Leave the yellow cells you do not use empty.
Open the Start sheet and type your household name, how you are paid, your next payday and the cash floor of your joint account. These drive every check.
Fill Bills with every bill, its due day, amount and autopay, then add its due dates in Bills Due. The next due date, price change and cost per paycheck fill in by themselves.
Pay-day routine: on each payday mark the bills paid since the last one in Bills Due, open Unpaid Before Payday and Payday Cover Check, and move money in if the balance would go under your floor.
Check Bills Calendar every week for the next 14 days and the Late and Missed list for anything open; use the late bill chaser and the messages for the call or text.
Fill Subscriptions with the price, renewal date, the date you last used each one and the price 6 months ago. Subscription Ranking, Unused Subscriptions and Subscription Creep fill in by themselves.
Mark each subscription Keep, Review or Cancel, then use Cancel Savings Calculator to see the saving a year. It is an estimate from your numbers, not a promise.
Fill Contracts with insurance, utility, phone, rent and loan contracts; Contract Review List and the review alert tell you when to ask for a better price before a renewal.
Month-close routine: mark every bill paid or late, read Bills by Month and the price changes, check the subscription charges, then plan the yearly bills due in the next 90 days.
Use the 18 tools, print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
A single adult with one income and no children can use every sheet here unchanged: leave partner 2 empty and ignore the shared rows in other parts of this suite.
Why a workbook: one flat price, no yearly renewal, your data stays with you and nothing to link or re-connect. It takes typed or pasted data and has no macros; it works in Excel and Google Sheets.
What this is not: not a bank app, not tax, legal, investment or credit advice. Every verdict is an estimate from your numbers; targets are your own, a typical range, check your own numbers.

listing.title: Household Bills and Subscriptions Tracker Excel Template: Bills Calendar, Due Dates, Subscription Audit, Contract Renewals
listing.headline: Never miss a bill: calendar, cash before payday, subscriptions and renewals
listing.description:
Run the bills side of your household money in one Excel workbook. Built for a single adult, a couple or a family who pay bills from a joint account, want to see what is due before the next payday and are tired of subscription apps with bank links that break. Bills holds every bill with its due day, amount, autopay and contact; Bills Due holds every due date for two years back and one year ahead with its status and the day it was paid. Bills Calendar shows the next bills in date order, and Unpaid Before Payday sets the open bills against your joint balance and your own cash floor.

Late and Missed ranks the worst late payments. Autopay Map shows which bills are on autopay and which land just before payday. Price Changes ranks the bills that rose against a year ago. Subscriptions lists every subscription with its price, renewal date and the day you last used it. Subscription Ranking, Unused Subscriptions, Renewals and Subscription Creep turn that list into a decision: keep, review or cancel, with the saving a year as an estimate from your numbers. Contracts, Insurance Calendar and Contract Review List remind you to review insurance, utility, phone, rent and loan contracts before they renew.

18 tools answer the weekly questions: will the balance cover the bills before payday, which late bill comes first, which manual bills move to autopay, what to set aside per paycheck, which subscriptions to cancel, whether subscriptions are creeping up and which contract to review next. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to a partner, a landlord, a utility company, an insurance agent, a bank branch, a school office or a subscription provider.

This is part two of the Household Finance suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros, one flat price and no yearly renewal, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. It works in Excel and Google Sheets. It helps you keep track of your bills and does not give tax, legal, investment or credit advice or promise results.

We would like to understand the reason for the rise and ask whether a better price or another plan is possible. Please let us know what you can offer.
Thank you for your time. We look forward to your reply.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own household.

documents.title: Due date change request letter
paragraphs: Dear {col:bills.contact}, this is {set:household}, dated {today}.

We pay {col:bills.bill}, {col:bills.amount}, on day {col:bills.due_day} of the month. Our income arrives around {set:next_payday}, so we would like to ask whether the due date can move to day {col:bills.new_day}.
Please tell us what is possible and from which date. We will keep paying on time.
Thank you for your help.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own household.

documents.title: Bills summary for the year
paragraphs: Bills summary of {set:household}, dated {today}. Month: {col:bills_month.month}. Bills due: {col:bills_month.bills_due}, paid on time: {col:bills_month.paid_on_time}, paid late: {col:bills_month.paid_late}. Total amount: {col:bills_month.total_amount}.
Last 12 months: {col:bills_month.year_bills} bills, {col:bills_month.year_total} in total, {col:bills_month.year_late} paid late.
Keep this page with your records. It shows what the bills cost and how reliably they were paid; it is not tax, legal or credit advice.
